messages:
jamal: FYI onboarding ticket from ACME — they're behind a corporate outbound proxy + strict firewall. They asked for exact IPs to open for our API (ticket #ACME-78).

maria-ops: Short answer: hostname-based allowlisting is preferable. Long answer: we publish region-specific source CIDR blocks but customers need to expect SNAT/NAT rotation and ephemeral source changes. If they can do FQDNs + SNI, that's the most robust.

alex: If they absolutely must use IPs, give them the region CIDRs we publish (example only): `35.201.0.0/16`, `34.90.0.0/16`. Call out that those CIDRs can change during infrastructure updates — we rotate some pools on a 24h cadence in certain regions.

maria-ops: Also warn them about proxy TLS interception. If the customer's proxy does TLS-inspect, the proxy must preserve SNI and the `:authority` header for HTTP/2; otherwise streaming (server-sent events / HTTP/2 sessions) will fail. Recommend they allow our hostnames without rewriting.

jamal: Their proxy team said they rewrite host headers for outbound requests and only support IP-based allowlists. What's best practice to avoid breakage?

alex: Two pragmatic options: 1) Allow our published IP ranges + open outbound TCP 443 to those ranges; OR 2) Allow DNS-resolved hostnames and configure the proxy to pass CONNECT through without header rewrites. Option 2 is preferable if possible.

maria-ops: Minimum rules to share with them: `- Outbound TCP 443 to api.redwood-inference.com and *.svc.redwood-inference.com`
`- Allow outbound DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to their resolver(s)`
`- Allow ephemeral return ports (1024-65535) for NATed connections`
`- If using a proxy, ensure CONNECT to 443 is allowed and TLS is not terminated/re-signed for our traffic unless they import our CA AND verify HTTP/2 headers are preserved.`

alex: If they're fingerprinting by source port or forcing narrow port ranges, streaming may break. If port restrictions are unavoidable, allow 443 and 8443. Websocket/streaming clients use long-lived connections; proxy timeouts must be increased (keepalive ~120s recommended).

jamal: Can you give me a short blurb I can paste into their change request?

maria-ops: Paste this: "Please allow outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) to api.redwood-inference.com and our regional service hostnames. If your security policy requires IP-level rules, allow the current regional CIDRs published at https://status.redwood.ai/egress and be aware these CIDRs may change on rotation — coordinate with Redwood before enforcing strict permanent rules. If you run a TLS-inspecting proxy, ensure it preserves SNI and HTTP/2 pseudo-headers and imports any internal CA used for interception. For streaming workloads, set proxy idle timeouts >= 120s and allow ephemeral return ports (1024-65535)."

alex: Also helpful to include a quick validation curl they can run from behind their proxy/NAT to confirm connectivity: 
```
# Replace <egress-ip> with one of the allowed source IPs or a resolver trick
curl -v --resolve api.redwood-inference.com:443:34.90.12.34 https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
```

srebot: NOTE: Our engineering team publishes daily snapshots of the active egress pools to https://status.redwood.ai/egress (json). We also post planned pool changes to the customer-notify webhook 48h in advance. NAT rotation windows: some regions rotate every 24h; dedicated customers have static SNATs if on Dedicated/Private deployments.

jamal: Perfect. I'll send that back to ACME and ask their proxy team to test the curl. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
